title: the visitor who came at night
hookLine: the altar call at camp, and a phrase that's older than any altar call
carry: never too old to start again
tomorrow: under the water and back up

cards: The music slows down. Every head bowed, every eye closed. The speaker says: if you want to give your life to Jesus tonight, raise your hand, or come forward.
Some people walked down that aisle at summer camp, some in a stadium, some never did. The phrase people used afterward was born again. That phrase is much older than any altar call.
It comes from a conversation at night.

teach.b: A respected teacher named Nicodemus comes to Jesus after dark. Jesus tells him: "Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God."
The Greek word for again, anothen, has a second meaning: from above. Nicodemus hears the first one and asks the obvious question: "How can a man be born when he is old?" Climb back into the womb?
Jesus means the second: a birth from above, by God's Spirit, which he compares to the wind. You can't see where it comes from; you only hear it.
A few lines later comes the verse on the signs at football games, John 3:16: "For God so loved the world."
The altar call itself is much newer. Revival preachers in the 1800s began inviting people to come forward, and big stadium crusades made it well-known.
Ask Jesus into your heart isn't a Bible phrase either; it's a simple way churches put it. And churches differ on how new birth happens: in a moment of decision, in baptism, over a lifetime.
But notice the picture Jesus chose. Nobody gives birth to themselves.

how: Many evangelical and Pentecostal Christians describe being born again as a moment of turning to Christ, sometimes at an altar call or by praying a short prayer; Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran and other churches connect new birth closely with baptism and a lifelong turning toward God.

games.q: who and what — tap the pairs.

s: in Jesus's words, born again can also mean born from above
the Greek word anothen means both.
the altar call goes back to the first Christians
it grew out of revival meetings in the 1800s.
he asked how a grown man could be born when he is old.

games.q: Jesus tells a respected teacher he must be born again. what does the teacher ask?
o: how can a man be born when he is old?
which day should I be baptized?
games.why: he takes it literally. Jesus means a birth from above, by the Spirit, like the wind you hear but can't see.

games.q: the Greek word anothen means two things. build both.

practice: Three breaths with the bell. On the first, think of something in your life that feels tired or stuck. On the second, notice you can't force it to be new, any more than a baby can give birth to itself.
On the third, just leave a little room for something new to come.

wordCard.voice: Born again. In the Greek of the story, born from above, too. Third word.

orig.note: Greek: again, anew, or from above. Jesus's word to Nicodemus carries both.

carryVoice: Your line: never too old to start again. It answers the question Nicodemus asked that night. That's day three.
